::: {.why}
A more flexible model produces a less stable forecast, which produces more turnover, which costs money, and that chain is where most machine learning advantages in this field disappear.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Report gross and net performance for every model and the turnover that separates them.
- Say what constraint you would add to make the flexible model competitive net, and test it.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>65 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Report the full picture: for every model, gross information ratio, turnover, net information ratio, and the net-Sharpe-against-cost curve on one axis. The flexible models will have higher turnover and the ordering may reverse between the gross and net columns.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Test one fix rather than several: add a turnover penalty to the portfolio construction, tuned on the validation period rather than the test period, and rerun. Report whether it closes the gap. Note that this is one more specification and log it, since the audit's trial count now includes it.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Compute the capacity of the winning model's portfolio using the same method as day 173, so the comparison against the alpha book is like for like.
:::
:::

::: {.deliverable}
Gross and net results with turnover for every model, the cost curve on one axis, and the turnover penalty tested.
:::

## Checkpoint

::: {.checkpoint}
Your boosting model wins gross by 20 percent and loses net. What is the mechanism, and did the turnover penalty fix it?
:::
